newsitem.title: SPAIN: Privatisation will cut ZCCM costs - consultant.
newsitem.headline: Privatisation will cut ZCCM costs - consultant.

text.p: Privatisation of Zambian mining giant, Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) will lead to lower operating costs, Dr Eckart Helmer, a consultant at the Zambia Privatisation Agency said.

"With improvement and investment, most of the underground mines will be competitive to other countries, although not with CODELCO," Helmer said at Metal Bulletin's 10th International Copper Conference.
ZCCM has the benefits of high grade orebodies, as well as very low energy costs, he said.
Meanwhile, trade unions in Zambia have been involved in the progress towards privatisation so far.
"They are 100 percent behind us, so we do not expect very much trouble from the unions," he said.

When the mines are sold off, responsibility for infrastructure, such as roads, water supplies and local facilities will switch to the government. Zambia is currently short of revenue to address these problems at present, Helmer said.
